# Run 1 (world: The Free Cities)
Session open. Chapter 2. Approval: autopilot. Spoilers: off.

## Changed since last session
Nothing changed since the last session.

## Settings
- as of: Spring, year 300
- genre: low fantasy
- tone: grim
- difficulty: balanced
- length: standard
- pacing: balanced
- dice: GM rolls
- turn_length: standard
- lines: harm to children
- veils: sexual content

## Voice anchor
Interior level: deep
Clipped, close third person, past tense. Plain diction, hard edges, dry humor; violence quick and ugly.

Sample:
> Rain came off the Black Wall in sheets, and the squire counted coins he didn't have.

## Open threads
- A knighthood if the city falls: Rickard's promise to Marro.
- Lissa's letter: Marro must carry it to her mother in the Dragon's Den.
- Pallo's debt: 30 silver stags due at the new moon.
- Who is selling the company?: The Triarch seems to know the company's plans.

## Chapters
- ch-01 The Black Wall: Rickard is wounded, Brother Olyvar dies of fever, Marro kills Dagna in self-defense and loses his dagger, and the company's grain now comes on the Triarch's credit.

## Rulings
- "Marro can read; his mother taught him."

- [Rickard Snow](characters/rickard-snow.md): Sellsword captain of the Golden Company, camped outside Volantis. A crossbow bolt wound in his left shoulder (ch-01): he can't raise a shield or draw a bow with that arm.

# Vaela Maegyr (character, vaela-maegyr, source: invention)
Aliases: Lady Vaela, the Maegyr widow

A widow of House Maegyr, of the Old Blood, who keeps a manse inside the Black Wall. In spring of year 300 she invited Rickard Snow to a feast at her house.

## Role [campaign]
Old Blood hostess; sits at the edge of Volantene politics and collects useful men.

## Motive [campaign]
Wants the Golden Company's sword pointed where House Maegyr finds it useful.

## Wants from the PC [campaign]
Nothing yet; sees him as Rickard's servant, and watches who Rickard trusts.

## Attitude to the PC [campaign]
Indifferent, faintly amused.

## Manner of speech [campaign]
Slow, soft High Valyrian-flavoured Common; answers questions with questions; never says a name she can avoid saying.

---

She knows who Rickard's mother was, and invited him because of it. She has not said so in front of anyone.

# Old Blood quarter (place, old-blood-quarter, source: invention)

## Vaela Maegyr (character, vaela-maegyr) aka Lady Vaela, the Maegyr widow
A widow of House Maegyr, of the Old Blood, who keeps a manse inside the Black Wall. In spring of year 300 she invited Rickard Snow to a feast at her house.
### Role [campaign]
Old Blood hostess; sits at the edge of Volantene politics and collects useful men.
### Motive [campaign]
Wants the Golden Company's sword pointed where House Maegyr finds it useful.

Indifferent, faintly amused.

Slow, soft High Valyrian-flavoured Common; answers questions with questions; never says a name she can avoid saying.

input.summary: Rickard took Hesse and Marro as escort to a feast at the manse of Vaela Maegyr, an Old Blood widow inside the Black Wall, without explaining how he knew her. Vaela withdrew with Rickard behind a curtain. A seating card named Marro, though no one had given his name; one of Pallo's grey-coated men, attending the grain factor Qavo, watched him. Hesse asked why a Maegyr would host a bastard sellsword; Marro said he didn't know, and Hesse hinted he should eavesdrop with a wine jug.

updates.body: Vaela Maegyr of the Old Blood invited Rickard Snow to a feast at her manse inside the Black Wall and greeted him as someone she knew, holding his hand too long. Rickard has told no one how he knows her, and no one in her hall says his name aloud.

Vaela Maegyr's steward wears a green livery and carries a token on a chain that passes guests through the Black Wall gate. Her porter takes escorts' weapons at the door: Hesse's sword and Marro's cudgel were left on a shelf there during the feast.

The feast's seating card, in the trade tongue, named 'Marro, squire' at the lower table by the fountain, though no one gave his name at the gate or in the hall. It named Rickard only as 'her guest from beyond the Wall'.
One of Pallo's grey-coated men attended the grain factor Qavo at Vaela Maegyr's feast. He recognised Marro and raised his cup to him like a creditor.

At the feast Hesse asked Marro why a Maegyr would invite a bastard sellsword, pressed him on what a squire hears, and hinted he should carry a wine jug past the curtain to listen. Marro said he didn't know.

thread_changes.title: Rickard and the Maegyr widow
thread_changes.body: Why does an Old Blood Maegyr host a bastard sellsword, and what did they say behind the curtain? Hesse wants to know too.

thread_changes.title: Who gave the house Marro's name?
thread_changes.body: The seating card named Marro though no one gave his name. Pallo's man was in the hall.
